Textless variant cover of _Green Arrow_ (vol. 6) No. 1 (August 2016). Art by [Neal Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neal_Adams "Neal Adams").

In 2016, DC relaunched its entire line of titles once again with the [DC Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Rebirth "DC Rebirth") event, this time intending to restore elements from the DC Universe prior to _Flashpoint_, while also maintaining the continuity of the New 52.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-30) Ben Percy remained the principal writer for the series, with a rotating art team consisting of Otto Schmidt, [Juan Ferreyra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Ferreyra?action=edit&redlink=1 "Juan Ferreyra (page does not exist)") and [Stephen Byrne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Byrne_(comics) "Stephen Byrne (comics)"). During this run, Green Arrow is seemingly betrayed by Emiko as Percy reintroduces [Shado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shado_(comics) "Shado (comics)"), echoing elements from the Grell run, as well as [John Diggle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Diggle_(Arrowverse) "John Diggle (Arrowverse)"). In addition to restoring Green Arrow's trademark Van Dyke beard, the series revisited a romance between Green Arrow and Black Canary for the first time since 2011. Percy also reestablished Green Arrow as a politically conscious figure, with the writer describing him as a "[social justice warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_justice_warrior "Social justice warrior")".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-31) After it was revealed that Emiko was still on Oliver's side, she eventually adopted the codename of _Red Arrow_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-32)

This volume finished in March 2019, with issue No. 50 serving as an extra sized final issue.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-33)

### Dawn of DC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Dawn of DC")]

In November 2022, it was announced that [Joshua Williamson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Williamson "Joshua Williamson") would write a new Green Arrow series following Oliver's disappearance at the end of [_Dark Crisis on Infinite Earths_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Crisis "Dark Crisis"), with Sean Izaakse illustrating and launching in April 2023.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-34) On April 25, the day of the first issue's release, it was announced that the initial six-issue miniseries would become a twelve-issue maxiseries.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-35)

Oliver eventually reunites with [Connor Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connor_Hawke "Connor Hawke"), [Roy Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Harper_(character) "Roy Harper (character)"), [Black Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Canary "Black Canary"), Red Canary, and Liam Harper after defeating Merlyn. Oliver has seemingly worked with [Amanda Waller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Waller "Amanda Waller") and starts arresting his family.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-36) During his work with Waller, he digs up a box that seemingly makes him regain his memory. It is revealed that [Martian Manhunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martian_Manhunter "Martian Manhunter") realized Amanda Waller's plans to make the world hate [metahumans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metahuman "Metahuman"), so he agreed to create a telepathic implant which will make Ollie fully believe in Waller's goals. Oliver helps disable the Amazon bots and the heroes regain their powers. In the aftermath, Oliver explains he had to do it because the Justice League disbanded so quickly when the Titans were not ready for future loose ends. He then further states that if they all had been more communicative as they did in the past, the events of Absolute Power would never had happened. [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman"), [Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman"), and [Wonder Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_Woman "Wonder Woman") begrudgingly agree with Oliver's reasonings and tell Oliver that they are bringing back the Justice League.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-37)

As with other DC superheroes, Green Arrow has an extensive supporting cast of characters, sometimes called **Team Arrow**, along with a unique [rogues gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogues_gallery "Rogues gallery") of villains. His supporting cast has changed wildly over the course of the series, but has tended to include his sidekick [Speedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_(comics) "Speedy (comics)") ([Roy Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Harper_(character) "Roy Harper (character)") and [Mia Dearden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_Dearden "Mia Dearden")) and his fellow superhero and main romantic interest, [Black Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Canary "Black Canary"). His son [Connor Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connor_Hawke "Connor Hawke") has also been a part of the Arrow vigilante family, along with Black Canary's adopted daughter [Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin_(DC_Comics) "Sin (DC Comics)"). For a brief time, Green Arrow was also "assisted" by the aspiring superhero [Miss Arrowette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowette "Arrowette"), with whom he had a brief affair. The New 52 reboot of Green Arrow has also introduced a number of new supporting characters for Oliver, including ex-Queen Industries technology experts Naomi Singh and Henry Fyff, and his archer half-sister [Emiko Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiko_Queen "Emiko Queen") who later takes up the code-name _Red Arrow_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-38) The characters of [Felicity Smoak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felicity_Smoak "Felicity Smoak") and [John Diggle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Diggle_(Arrowverse) "John Diggle (Arrowverse)") from the _Arrow_ TV series were also adapted into the comic books in 2015 (though Felicity was later removed from the continuity). The archer [Shado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shado_(comics) "Shado (comics)"), though not part of Oliver's unit of heroes, has also been a recurring character in Oliver's life. Additionally, Green Arrow has been regularly paired with his fellow superhero [Green Lantern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Lantern "Green Lantern") ([Hal Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hal_Jordan "Hal Jordan")) in comics, as the two co-starred in the series _Green Lantern/Green Arrow_ together for many years. The _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ version of Team Arrow include [Roy Harper/Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Harper_(Arrowverse) "Roy Harper (Arrowverse)"), [Sara Lance/White Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Lance "Sara Lance"), [Thea Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thea_Queen "Thea Queen")/Speedy, [Laurel Lance/Black Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurel_Lance_(Arrowverse) "Laurel Lance (Arrowverse)"), [Curtis Holt/Mister Terrific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtis_Holt_(Arrowverse) "Curtis Holt (Arrowverse)"), [Rene Ramirez/Wild Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rene_Ramirez "Rene Ramirez"), [Rory Regan/Ragman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_Regan_(Arrowverse) "Rory Regan (Arrowverse)"), [Evelyn Sharp/Artemis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Sharp_(Arrowverse) "Evelyn Sharp (Arrowverse)") and [Dinah Drake/Black Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinah_Drake_(Arrowverse) "Dinah Drake (Arrowverse)").

As a [Justice League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_League "Justice League") member, Green Arrow will also appear in crossovers with stories featuring other DC flagship characters from time to time. Of his Justice League colleagues, classic stories depict Ollie as having an ongoing feud with [Hawkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawkman "Hawkman") owing to their differing outlooks on life, and more recently, he has been depicted as a good friend of his [Justice League United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_League_United "Justice League United") colleague [Animal Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Man "Animal Man"). Green Arrow has also been a member of the [Outsiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outsiders_(comics) "Outsiders (comics)"), both in its incarnation as a covert superhero team led by [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman") and in its New 52 form as a [secret society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_society "Secret society") based around various weapon clans, including an Arrow Clan which Oliver is the rightful head of. In the [Golden Age of Comic Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Age_of_Comic_Books "Golden Age of Comic Books"), Green Arrow and Speedy were also affiliated with the superhero group the [Seven Soldiers of Victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Soldiers_of_Victory "Seven Soldiers of Victory").

Recurring Green Arrow villains of course include his archenemies [Merlyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merlyn_(DC_Comics) "Merlyn (DC Comics)"), a master archer, and [Count Vertigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count_Vertigo "Count Vertigo"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-39) a foreign dignitary with the power to disrupt his enemy's balance and perception. ### Earth-Two

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Earth-Two")]

See also: [Crisis on Infinite Earths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis_on_Infinite_Earths "Crisis on Infinite Earths") and [Multiverse (DC Comics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiverse_(DC_Comics) "Multiverse (DC Comics)")

For many years, DC Comics wrote stories in what it called a [multiverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiverse "Multiverse"), or a series of infinite parallel Earths. This allowed DC writers to freely [retcon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retcon "Retcon") and retell stories, as well as explain continuity mistakes. The Green Arrow of the 1940s, like all [Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Age_of_Comic_Books "Golden Age of Comic Books") characters at that time, resided on [Earth-Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth-Two "Earth-Two") and was a member of the [Seven Soldiers of Victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Soldiers_of_Victory "Seven Soldiers of Victory") and [All-Star Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Star_Squadron "All-Star Squadron") along with his sidekick [Speedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Harper_(character) "Roy Harper (character)"). Despite having a different origin than the modern Green Arrow, the Golden Age character's development largely parallels the modern one's. In _[Crisis on Infinite Earths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis\_on\_Infinite\_Earths "Crisis on Infinite Earths")_, the multiverse is destroyed and Green Arrow is retroactively erased.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-42)

### Modern DC alternate universes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Modern DC alternate universes")]

DC's weekly series _[52](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/52\_(comics) "52 (comics)")_ established a new 52-Earth [Multiverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiverse_(DC_Comics) "Multiverse (DC Comics)"). The ongoing series _[Countdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countdown\_(DC\_Comics) "Countdown (DC Comics)")_ showcased several of these. On Earth-3, an evil equivalent of Oliver Queen is a member of the supervillain co-op called the [Crime Society of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_Syndicate "Crime Syndicate"). Another evil equivalent exists in the [Antimatter Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antimatter_universe_of_Qward "Antimatter universe of Qward") called **Deadeye**. On Earth-15, Roy Harper has replaced Oliver as Green Arrow.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-43) In the gender-reversed world of Earth-11, Oliver is now Olivia Queen, and that world's version of the Black Canary closely resembles him in appearance.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-44) The _Kingdom Come_ (Earth-22) and _Dark Knight Returns_ (Earth-31) stories and their variations of Oliver were later amalgamated into the 52-Earth Multiverse.

In the alternate timeline of the _[Flashpoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashpoint\_(comics) "Flashpoint (comics)")_ event, Oliver Queen is the head of Green Arrow Industries, a major military contracting company, as well as leads an ex-military band of Green Arrows. Even though Oliver is an inventive genius, he steals advanced gadgets from super-villains for military use. Oliver discovers his Green Arrows were killed by a female raider at his base at [Starfish Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starfish_Island_(DC_Comics) "Starfish Island (DC Comics)") and killing his best friend/head of security Roy Harper. Taking his weapons and gadgets to hunt down the woman in battle, Oliver shockingly learns that she is a daughter of his and [Vixen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vixen_(character) "Vixen (character)"), Oliver's former lover, as well as the reason she attacked him was because Green Arrow Industries built factories which specializing in testing super-villain weapons in American towns that inadvertently became targets for the super-villains looking to gain their weapons back. Shocked by her revelation, Oliver had only been stalling before his daughter is killed by his reserve teams he earlier called.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-45)

### Earth-31/_The Dark Knight Returns_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Earth-31/The Dark Knight Returns")]

The character appears in [Frank Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Miller "Frank Miller")'s _[Batman: The Dark Knight Returns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_The\_Dark\_Knight\_Returns "Batman: The Dark Knight Returns")_ and the sequel _[Batman: The Dark Knight Strikes Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_The\_Dark\_Knight\_Strikes\_Again "Batman: The Dark Knight Strikes Again")_ listed as [Earth-31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth-31 "Earth-31"). Despite missing an arm (implied to be because of [Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman")),[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-46) Oliver still proves to be an effective archer, grasping the nocks of his arrows in his teeth. After Batman fakes his death for him to go underground, Oliver, sporting a mechanical arm, joins Batman in his war against [Alexander Luthor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Luthor "Lex Luthor")'s government. In _The Dark Knight Returns_, Oliver is portrayed as an anarchist, while in _The Dark Knight Strikes Again_, he is explicitly described as a "billionaire turned [Communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist "Communist")."[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-47)

### Other DC Elseworlds stories

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Other DC Elseworlds stories")]

In _[JLA: The Nail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JLA:\_The\_Nail "JLA: The Nail")_ and [its sequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JLA:_Another_Nail "JLA: Another Nail"), Oliver is a featured as a disabled ex-hero, having lost an arm, an eye, and the use of his legs in a fight with [Amazo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazo "Amazo"), which also resulted in the death of [Hawkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawkman "Hawkman"). Bitter and furious, he now spreads fear on [Perry White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perry_White "Perry White")'s talk show about the JLA being aliens and claims that they are planning to conquer the world; his former teammates speculate that this is his method of coping.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-48) In the sequel, Oliver's brain is transplanted into Amazo's body–the Flash having removed Amazo's computerized brain in an earlier fight–restoring his sanity, allowing him to defeat the creature threatening the universe at the cost of his own life, after mending fences with his former teammates.

In _[Batman: Holy Terror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_Holy\_Terror "Batman: Holy Terror")_, Oliver Queen is mentioned as having been executed, found guilty of supporting underground Jewish "pornographers".[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-49) He has a cameo as Bruce Wayne's society friend in Dean Motter's _[Batman: Nine Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_Nine\_Lives "Batman: Nine Lives")_.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-50) Oliver Queen also appears in [Mike Mignola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Mignola "Mike Mignola")'s _[Batman: The Doom That Came to Gotham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_The\_Doom\_That\_Came\_to\_Gotham "Batman: The Doom That Came to Gotham")_, where he is portrayed as a guilt-ridden latter-day [Templar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights_Templar "Knights Templar") equipped with magic arrows dipped in the blood of [Saint Sebastian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Sebastian "Saint Sebastian"). He is killed in issue No. 2 by [Poison Ivy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poison_Ivy_(character) "Poison Ivy (character)").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-51) Oliver appears in _[Superman: Red Son](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman:\_Red\_Son "Superman: Red Son")_, where Oliver Queen is a reporter for the _[Daily Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily\_Planet "Daily Planet")_ working underneath [Perry White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perry_White "Perry White") and eventually [Lois Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lois_Lane "Lois Lane").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-52)

An older, balding Green Arrow appears in [Mark Waid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Waid "Mark Waid") and [Alex Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Ross "Alex Ross")' futuristic _[Kingdom Come](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom\_Come\_(comics) "Kingdom Come (comics)")_, in which Oliver has joined forces with Batman to oppose Superman's army/Justice League. He married his longtime love [Dinah Lance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinah_Lance "Dinah Lance") and they have a daughter, **Olivia Queen** aka **Black Canary**.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-53)

Green Arrow appears in _League of Justice_, a _[The Lord of the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lord\_of\_the\_Rings "The Lord of the Rings")_–inspired fantasy where the character is renamed "**Longbow Greenarrow**": a mysterious wizard resembling [Gandalf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandalf "Gandalf"). _JLA: Age of Wonder_ shows Green Arrow as a defender of the poor and an enemy of oppression.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-54)

### _Injustice_ series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Injustice series")]

In the _[Injustice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injustice:\_Gods\_Among\_Us\_(comics) "Injustice: Gods Among Us (comics)")_ universe, where the [Joker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_(character) "Joker (character)") kills Lois Lane and her unborn child, Green Arrow joins Batman's Insurgency against Superman's Regime, recognizing Superman's harsher approach to ending crime following his loss. In _[Injustice: Gods Among Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injustice:\_Gods\_Among\_Us\_(comics) "Injustice: Gods Among Us (comics)")_, Green Arrow is married to [Black Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Canary "Black Canary") and also unintentionally becomes close to [Harley Quinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harley_Quinn "Harley Quinn"), who he saves from a near-death encounter with Superman. Near the end of Year One (the comic's first volume) he is mortally wounded by Superman in his Fortress of Solitude after the former mistakenly believes that the Insurgency has come to harm [Jonathan and Martha Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_and_Martha_Kent "Jonathan and Martha Kent"). Before dying, Green Arrow delivers the super pills to the Insurgency. Year Two reveals Black Canary to be pregnant with Green Arrow's child, leaving her determined to take down Superman for his murder.

*   When Superman nearly kills Black Canary trying to avenge Green Arrow, Doctor Fate heals and takes Dinah to an alternate universe where a different version of Oliver Queen remains alive but his own Black Canary, along with most of his allies, are deceased. Doctor Fate leaves the two to raise the baby—named [Conner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connor_Hawke "Connor Hawke")—together, giving each other a chance at happiness. Five years later, in the prequel comic of the game's sequel _[Injustice 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injustice\_2\_(comics) "Injustice 2 (comics)")_, the alternate Oliver and Dinah receive news from Doctor Fate of Superman's defeat at the hands of his Prime-Earth counterpart. While Dinah is brought home by Doctor Fate to help Batman restore Earth, the alternate Oliver joins in to honor his late-counterpart. The alternate Oliver discovers that, unlike himself, his deceased counterpart maintained his wealth and resources, and while the public is unaware that its Oliver Queen is dead, alternate Green Arrow is able to access them for the heroes' needs. He learns his counterpart's marriage to Dinah, prompting her to ask the alternate Green Arrow his hand-in-marriage, which he accepts. He and Batman also do not get along, waiting for an opportunity to duel after Oliver reveals that, based on what he learned from Dinah, he has more training than his counterpart.

### Superman: American Alien

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Superman: American Alien")]

In the 2016 comic book _[Superman: American Alien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman:\_American\_Alien "Superman: American Alien")_ by [Max Landis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Landis "Max Landis"), which features an alternate retelling of Clark's journey to becoming Superman, Oliver Queen encounters [Clark Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman") two times in his life. First is when Clark was nineteen and Oliver mistakes him for [Bruce Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman "Batman"), whom he had thrown a birthday party for despite being aware that Wayne would never show up. Clark, after some hesitation, decides to enjoy himself and befriends Oliver, though he briefly becomes annoyed and shocked at how much money Oliver and his friends waste. Years later, after getting off Starfish Island, Oliver has matured more and encounters Clark again, who has begun his new career at the Daily Planet. At first believing him to be Bruce, Clark quickly comes clean. Oliver forgives him before introducing him to [Lex Luthor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Luthor "Lex Luthor"), partly to annoy the latter.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-55)

### Earth 2

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Earth 2")]

In the pages of _[Earth 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth-Two "Earth-Two"): World's End_, Oliver Queen is an ally of Batman and operates as Red Arrow. When Batman was killed during the [Apokoliptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apokolips "Apokolips") invasion, Red Arrow continued to guard the Codex, which contained the DNA of every organism on Earth, in an underwater fortress built by Bruce Wayne. When [Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Wayne "Thomas Wayne") and [Huntress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntress_(Helena_Wayne) "Huntress (Helena Wayne)") arrive at the underwater fortress, they meet Red Arrow, who assists in fighting the second Apokoliptian invasion. Red Arrow and the Codex are evacuated from Earth before it is destroyed.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-56)

### Absolute Universe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Green_Arrow&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Absolute Universe")]

Two versions of Green Arrow appear in the [Absolute Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_Universe "Absolute Universe"), otherwise known as **Alpha World**, a universe corrupted by Darkseid's energy. In this world, Oliver Queen is a self-made billionaire who developed a trading app with his friend Jubal Slade, who he later cut ties with once he discovers Jubal's sexual misconduct. Years later, Oliver discovers Jubal's human trafficking operation on a remote island and plans to become a vigilante archer to take him down. However, his plans are discovered by the Justice League, who send [Carter Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Hall_(comics) "Carter Hall (comics)") to assassinate him, ending his superhero career before it's begun.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-57)

Months later, a mysterious masked figure, dubbed **the Longbow Hunter**, appears wielding Oliver's gear and begins violently murdering corrupt billionaires connected to Oliver Queen, starting with Jubal Slade. Executive protection specialist and Oliver's ex-girlfriend, [Dinah Lance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinah_Lance "Dinah Lance"), is forcibly hired to investigate the Hunter and uncover his identity.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Arrow#cite_note-58)

**Stephen Adam Amell**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-1) (born May 8, 1981) is a Canadian-American actor. He came to prominence for playing the lead role of [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") on [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") superhero series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ (2012–2020), based on [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics"). Amell also appeared in subsequent [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse") franchise media, along with reprising his role in various video games. Following the conclusion of _Arrow_, Amell landed the lead roles in both the [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_ (2021–2023), and _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ (2025).

Outside of television, Amell portrayed [Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)") in the superhero film _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows")_ (2016). Amell co-produced and starred in _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_ and its sequel _[Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8:\_Part\_II "Code 8: Part II")_ with his cousin [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell"). He has also made a number of appearances in the [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") circuit.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Stephen Adam Amell was born on May 8, 1981,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-2) in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Ontario, the son of Sandra Anne (née Bolté) and Thomas J. Amell.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-4) He is a first cousin of actor [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-5) He attended [St. Andrew's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Andrew's_College,_Aurora "St. Andrew's College, Aurora"), a private independent school for boys, and graduated in 2000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-6)

## Acting career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Acting career")]

### 2004–2012: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2004–2012: Early career")]

Amell appeared in two episodes of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer_as_Folk_(season_4) "Queer as Folk (season 4)") of _[Queer as Folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer\_as\_Folk\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Queer as Folk (2000 TV series)")_ as the Liberty Ride spinning instructor in 2004. Amell played Adam in the first season of the television series _[Dante's Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dante's\_Cove "Dante's Cove")_; he was replaced in the second season by Jon Fleming. In 2007, Amell won a [Gemini Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_Awards "Gemini Awards") for his guest-starring role on _[ReGenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReGenesis "ReGenesis")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) The same year he was also nominated for a Gemini Award in the Best Ensemble Cast Category for _[Rent-a-Goalie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rent-a-Goalie "Rent-a-Goalie")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-8) He had recurring roles in the TV series _[Da Kink in My Hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Kink\_in\_My\_Hair\_(TV\_series) "Da Kink in My Hair (TV series)")_ and _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_. On December 3, 2010, Amell joined the cast of _[The Vampire Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vampire\_Diaries "The Vampire Diaries")_ as werewolf 'Brady' for season 2.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-9) Amell starred as the real life convicted killer [Joran van der Sloot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joran_van_der_Sloot "Joran van der Sloot") in the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") film _[Justice for Natalee Holloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_for\_Natalee\_Holloway "Justice for Natalee Holloway")_ which originally aired in May 2011.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10)

On October 2, 2011, season 3 of [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")'s series _[Hung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hung\_(TV\_series) "Hung (TV series)")_ premiered with Amell starring as busboy-turned-prostitute Jason, a younger rival "ho" to [Thomas Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jane "Thomas Jane")'s Ray Drecker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) He also appeared as Jim in the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210_(season_4) "90210 (season 4)") of _[90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210\_(TV\_series) "90210 (TV series)")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) Amell announced on October 28, 2011, that he had just finished filming the Christmas episode of _[New Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Girl "New Girl")_ with [Zooey Deschanel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooey_Deschanel "Zooey Deschanel") and [Max Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Greenfield "Max Greenfield"). He touches on the experience of filming his first "network half-hour comedy" in an interview with _Daemon's TV_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) On November 9, 2011, Amell was announced for the recurring role of Scottie, a paramedic on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _[Private Practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private\_Practice\_(TV\_series) "Private Practice (TV series)")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-12) He also played the role of Travis McKenna in _[Blue Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Mountain\_State "Blue Mountain State")_.

### 2012–2020: _Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2012–2020: Arrow")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg/250px-Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg)

Amell on the set of _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ in September 2014

In January 2012, Amell was cast as [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") in [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_, based on the [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") superhero of the same name.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10) This series and role led to Amell appearing as the character on other superhero series on the network as part of the growing [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse"), including _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(2014\_TV\_series) "The Flash (2014 TV series)")_, _[Legends of Tomorrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_Tomorrow "Legends of Tomorrow")_, _[Supergirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergirl\_(TV\_series) "Supergirl (TV series)")_, and _[Batwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batwoman\_(TV\_series) "Batwoman (TV series)")_, as well as the [CW Seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CW_Seed "CW Seed") webseries _[Vixen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vixen\_(web\_series) "Vixen (web series)")_.

Amell co-starred in _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows\_(film) "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows (film)")_ (released on June 3, 2016) as vigilante "[Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)")".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-13) Amell announced in May 2017 that he would be participating on a special celebrity edition of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-14) Amell demonstrated great physical abilities which was reflective of his athleticism in his portrayal of Oliver Queen.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-15) In 2017, he took part in the directorial debut of former _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_ co-star [Michelle Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Morgan_(actress) "Michelle Morgan (actress)"), a short film entitled _Mi Madre, My Father_, playing the estranged father of a six-year-old girl. Morgan raised funds for the production through a crowdfunding campaign.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Morgan-16) The film premiered at the 2018 [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Cannes-17)

In March 2019, Amell announced the end of _Arrow_ with its [eighth and final season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow_season_8 "Arrow season 8"), which premiered in October 2019 and concluded in January 2020.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-18)

### 2020–present: Post-_Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2020–present: Post-Arrow")]

His first post-_Arrow_ project was announced in August 2019 as _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_, a [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series set in the world of [independent professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_professional_wrestling "Independent professional wrestling").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-19) In December of the same year, it was announced that short-form streaming platform [Quibi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quibi "Quibi") were developing a spin-off series starring Amell and his cousin Robbie Amell, developed from their crowd-funded film _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-20) In September 2023, _Heels_ was canceled after two seasons.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-21) In February 2024, Stephen Amell was cast as Ted Black in the upcoming [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") pilot _Suits LA_, based on the [USA Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Network "USA Network") original series _[Suits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_(American\_TV\_series) "Suits (American TV series)")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-22) On July 19, 2024, _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ has ordered to series by NBC.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-23)

Amell plays Henry Roland, a police officer, in the [Crave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crave_(TV_network) "Crave (TV network)") crime drama series _[The Borderline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Borderline\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "The Borderline (Canadian TV series)")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-24) it debuted in February 2026.

He garnered positive reviews for his leading role in the Canadian crime film _[Little Lorraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little\_Lorraine "Little Lorraine")_, released in 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-25)

## Professional wrestling career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Professional wrestling career")]

### WWE (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: WWE (2015)")]

As an avid [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") fan,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell campaigned for a guest appearance on [WWE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE "WWE")'s weekly _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ program.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-27)

In May 2015, it was reported that he was set to wrestle [Stardust (Cody Rhodes)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") at WWE's [SummerSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SummerSlam_(2015) "SummerSlam (2015)") pay-per-view in August.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell made his first WWE appearance on the May 25 episode of _Raw_, where he had a confrontation with Stardust.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-28) Amell returned to _Raw_ in early August; after being assaulted in the audience by Stardust, Amell got into the [ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_ring "Wrestling ring") to attack him until being contained by security. Following a [backstage segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Segment "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") with [Triple H](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_H "Triple H"), it was announced that [Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neville_(wrestler) "Neville (wrestler)") would team with Amell to face Stardust and [King Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wade_Barrett "Wade Barrett") at SummerSlam.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-29)

At the event on August 23, 2015, Amell and Neville defeated Barrett and Stardust in a [tag team match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_tag_team_match_types "Professional wrestling tag team match types"). Amell participated in the wrestling, and, behind the scenes, wrestlers were said to have been impressed with Amell's performance.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-31) Amell became friends with Rhodes, with whom he later also worked on _Arrow_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-BulletClub-32)

On December 21, 2015, Amell was awarded a [Slammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slammy "Slammy") for the "Celebrity Moment of the Year" for his dive onto Stardust during the match.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-33)

### Ring of Honor (2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Ring of Honor (2017)")]

Amell returned to professional wrestling for [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") on November 17, 2017, at [Survival of the Fittest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survival_of_the_Fittest_(2017) "Survival of the Fittest (2017)").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-34) On the day of the show, Amell joined the [Bullet Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullet_Club "Bullet Club")[faction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Stable "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"), and teamed with Cody Rhodes, [Kenny Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Omega "Kenny Omega"), and [The Young Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Young_Bucks "The Young Bucks") (Matt and Nick Jackson) in a five-on-four tag team match. They defeated [The Addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Addiction_(professional_wrestling) "The Addiction (professional wrestling)") ([Christopher Daniels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Daniels "Christopher Daniels") and [Frankie Kazarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankie_Kazarian "Frankie Kazarian")), [Flip Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_Gordon "Flip Gordon"), and [Scorpio Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpio_Sky "Scorpio Sky"), and Amell again participated in the wrestling, including being put through a table by The Addiction.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-35)

### All In (2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: All In (2018)")]

On August 6, 2018, it was announced that Amell would be competing at [All In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_In_(professional_wrestling_event) "All In (professional wrestling event)"), in his first-ever singles match, where he was defeated by Christopher Daniels.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-36)

### All Elite Wrestling (2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: All Elite Wrestling (2020)")]

On February 29, 2020, Amell made an appearance at [All Elite Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Elite_Wrestling "All Elite Wrestling")'s [Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution_(2020) "Revolution (2020)"), where he accompanied [Cody Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") alongside Rhodes' [Nightmare Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightmare_Family "Nightmare Family") for his match against [MJF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Jacob_Friedman "Maxwell Jacob Friedman").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-37)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

Amell has hosted a number of successful fundraising campaigns via the crowd funded merchandise platform [Represent.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Represent.com "Represent.com").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-38) In 2014, Amell partnered with the charity Fuck Cancer to raise almost a million dollars with the release of a T-shirt featuring his face on the front (with a Post-it note on his forehead and featuring the organization's name). He ended up selling over 60,000 shirts from this campaign.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-39) In January 2015, Amell launched his second Represent.com campaign featuring a word he made up, _Sinceriously_, to benefit two mental health charities: Paws and Stripes and Stand For The Silent.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In August 2015, Amell used his guest appearance on _[WWE Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ with [Stardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") to raise funds via his third campaign for children's hospice Emily's House in Toronto. The campaign raised $300,000, and Amell and Stardust presented a cheque together at Emily's House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-40) During the Red Nose Day special of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_, Amell donated $35,000 for completing all six obstacles, and an extra obstacle, the Salmon Ladder.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-41)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Amell married his first wife, fellow Canadian Carolyn Lawrence, on December 8, 2007, in Toronto.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-42) The couple divorced in 2010.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-43) Amell married actress and model [Cassandra Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassandra_Jean "Cassandra Jean") on December 25, 2012, in a private ceremony in [the Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Caribbean "The Caribbean"),[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-44) and for a second time in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") on May 26, 2013.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-45) The couple have a daughter who was born on October 15, 2013. They have a son, born May 13, 2022.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-46) Amell revealed on his Instagram that he became a dual citizen of Canada and the United States and took his U.S. citizenship oath in August 2022 at Dodger Stadium.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-47)

Amell's statements and behavior have occasionally drawn controversy. In September 2015, after a [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") student was arrested for [bringing a disassembled digital clock to his high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Mohamed_clock_incident "Ahmed Mohamed clock incident") in [Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving,_Texas "Irving, Texas"), Texas, Amell tweeted, "Stereotyping Texas isn't any better than stereotyping Ahmed".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-48) The post drew criticism online, prompting Amell to take a break from social media.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-51)

In 2018, Amell tweeted "my âpölògīés"[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-52) in response to criticism about his failure to use the [acute accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acute_accent "Acute accent") while tweeting singer [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé")'s name.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-54) After he was accused by online commenters of disrespecting [black names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_names "African-American names"), he said he had omitted the accent while being "lazy in the midst of a mediocre joke".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-55)

In 2020, during the [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter")[protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests"), Amell was criticized by comic book writer [Tee Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tee_Franklin "Tee Franklin") and others for saying that racism is a systemic problem but that he had not personally "seen it in action".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-56)

In 2021, Amell was asked to leave a [Delta Air Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Air_Lines "Delta Air Lines") flight traveling from Austin to Los Angeles for yelling at his wife.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-57) He later said he was intoxicated at the time.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-59)

In July 2023, Amell was criticized for comments he made at a fan convention regarding the [2023 SAG-AFTRA strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SAG-AFTRA_strike "2023 SAG-AFTRA strike"). While he expressed support for [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA") as his union, he called striking a "reductive negotiating tactic" and "myopic" and seemed to criticize that the strike banned him from promoting the second season of _Heels_.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-61) He later clarified his opinion, saying that while he does not like striking, he "[understands] fundamentally why we're here" and stated that his support for the union was unconditional and that he stood with them.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-62) Amell did not attend the _Arrow_ cast reunion on the picket line outside the Warner Bros. studio lot in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"), as he was in New York City at the time, but on the day of the reunion, he was photographed on the picket line in front of the [Warner Bros. Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Discovery "Warner Bros. Discovery") offices in New York and reportedly sent his regards to his former showrunners in California. [Marc Guggenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Guggenheim "Marc Guggenheim"), executive producer of _Arrow_ and organizer of the revival, interpreted his attendance in New York as a symbolic stand in solidarity.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-64)

**Stephen Adam Amell**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-1) (born May 8, 1981) is a Canadian-American actor. He came to prominence for playing the lead role of [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") on [the CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") superhero series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ (2012–2020), based on [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics"). Amell also appeared in subsequent [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse") franchise media, along with reprising his role in various video games. Following the conclusion of _Arrow_, Amell landed the lead roles in both the [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_ (2021–2023), and _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ (2025).

Outside of television, Amell portrayed [Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)") in the superhero film _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows")_ (2016). Amell co-produced and starred in _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_ and its sequel _[Code 8: Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8:\_Part\_II "Code 8: Part II")_ with his cousin [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell"). He has also made a number of appearances in the [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") circuit.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Stephen Adam Amell was born on May 8, 1981,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-2) in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Ontario, the son of Sandra Anne (née Bolté) and Thomas J. Amell.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-4) He is a first cousin of actor [Robbie Amell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_Amell "Robbie Amell").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-5) He attended [St. Andrew's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Andrew's_College,_Aurora "St. Andrew's College, Aurora"), a private independent school for boys, and graduated in 2000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-6)

## Acting career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Acting career")]

### 2004–2012: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2004–2012: Early career")]

Amell appeared in two episodes of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer_as_Folk_(season_4) "Queer as Folk (season 4)") of _[Queer as Folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer\_as\_Folk\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Queer as Folk (2000 TV series)")_ as the Liberty Ride spinning instructor in 2004. Amell played Adam in the first season of the television series _[Dante's Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dante's\_Cove "Dante's Cove")_; he was replaced in the second season by Jon Fleming. In 2007, Amell won a [Gemini Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_Awards "Gemini Awards") for his guest-starring role on _[ReGenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReGenesis "ReGenesis")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) The same year he was also nominated for a Gemini Award in the Best Ensemble Cast Category for _[Rent-a-Goalie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rent-a-Goalie "Rent-a-Goalie")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-8) He had recurring roles in the TV series _[Da Kink in My Hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da\_Kink\_in\_My\_Hair\_(TV\_series) "Da Kink in My Hair (TV series)")_ and _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_. On December 3, 2010, Amell joined the cast of _[The Vampire Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vampire\_Diaries "The Vampire Diaries")_ as werewolf 'Brady' for season 2.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-9) Amell starred as the real life convicted killer [Joran van der Sloot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joran_van_der_Sloot "Joran van der Sloot") in the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") film _[Justice for Natalee Holloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_for\_Natalee\_Holloway "Justice for Natalee Holloway")_ which originally aired in May 2011.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10)

On October 2, 2011, season 3 of [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")'s series _[Hung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hung\_(TV\_series) "Hung (TV series)")_ premiered with Amell starring as busboy-turned-prostitute Jason, a younger rival "ho" to [Thomas Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jane "Thomas Jane")'s Ray Drecker.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Free-7) He also appeared as Jim in the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210_(season_4) "90210 (season 4)") of _[90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90210\_(TV\_series) "90210 (TV series)")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) Amell announced on October 28, 2011, that he had just finished filming the Christmas episode of _[New Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Girl "New Girl")_ with [Zooey Deschanel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooey_Deschanel "Zooey Deschanel") and [Max Greenfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Greenfield "Max Greenfield"). He touches on the experience of filming his first "network half-hour comedy" in an interview with _Daemon's TV_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-TV-11) On November 9, 2011, Amell was announced for the recurring role of Scottie, a paramedic on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _[Private Practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private\_Practice\_(TV\_series) "Private Practice (TV series)")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-12) He also played the role of Travis McKenna in _[Blue Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Mountain\_State "Blue Mountain State")_.

### 2012–2020: _Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2012–2020: Arrow")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg/250px-Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stephen_Amell_2014.jpg)

Amell on the set of _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_ in September 2014

In January 2012, Amell was cast as [Oliver Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Queen_(Arrowverse) "Oliver Queen (Arrowverse)") in [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Arrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow\_(TV\_series) "Arrow (TV series)")_, based on the [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") superhero of the same name.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-AV-10) This series and role led to Amell appearing as the character on other superhero series on the network as part of the growing [Arrowverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowverse "Arrowverse"), including _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(2014\_TV\_series) "The Flash (2014 TV series)")_, _[Legends of Tomorrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_Tomorrow "Legends of Tomorrow")_, _[Supergirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergirl\_(TV\_series) "Supergirl (TV series)")_, and _[Batwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batwoman\_(TV\_series) "Batwoman (TV series)")_, as well as the [CW Seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CW_Seed "CW Seed") webseries _[Vixen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vixen\_(web\_series) "Vixen (web series)")_.

Amell co-starred in _[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage\_Mutant\_Ninja\_Turtles:\_Out\_of\_the\_Shadows\_(film) "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows (film)")_ (released on June 3, 2016) as vigilante "[Casey Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casey_Jones_(Teenage_Mutant_Ninja_Turtles) "Casey Jones (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)")".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-13) Amell announced in May 2017 that he would be participating on a special celebrity edition of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-14) Amell demonstrated great physical abilities which was reflective of his athleticism in his portrayal of Oliver Queen.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-15) In 2017, he took part in the directorial debut of former _[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")_ co-star [Michelle Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Morgan_(actress) "Michelle Morgan (actress)"), a short film entitled _Mi Madre, My Father_, playing the estranged father of a six-year-old girl. Morgan raised funds for the production through a crowdfunding campaign.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Morgan-16) The film premiered at the 2018 [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-Cannes-17)

In March 2019, Amell announced the end of _Arrow_ with its [eighth and final season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrow_season_8 "Arrow season 8"), which premiered in October 2019 and concluded in January 2020.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-18)

### 2020–present: Post-_Arrow_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2020–present: Post-Arrow")]

His first post-_Arrow_ project was announced in August 2019 as _[Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heels\_(TV\_series) "Heels (TV series)")_, a [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz "Starz") drama series set in the world of [independent professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_professional_wrestling "Independent professional wrestling").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-19) In December of the same year, it was announced that short-form streaming platform [Quibi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quibi "Quibi") were developing a spin-off series starring Amell and his cousin Robbie Amell, developed from their crowd-funded film _[Code 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code\_8\_(2019\_film) "Code 8 (2019 film)")_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-20) In September 2023, _Heels_ was canceled after two seasons.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-21) In February 2024, Stephen Amell was cast as Ted Black in the upcoming [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") pilot _Suits LA_, based on the [USA Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Network "USA Network") original series _[Suits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_(American\_TV\_series) "Suits (American TV series)")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-22) On July 19, 2024, _[Suits LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suits\_LA "Suits LA")_ has ordered to series by NBC.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-23)

Amell plays Henry Roland, a police officer, in the [Crave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crave_(TV_network) "Crave (TV network)") crime drama series _[The Borderline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Borderline\_(Canadian\_TV\_series) "The Borderline (Canadian TV series)")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-24) it debuted in February 2026.

He garnered positive reviews for his leading role in the Canadian crime film _[Little Lorraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little\_Lorraine "Little Lorraine")_, released in 2026.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-25)

## Professional wrestling career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Professional wrestling career")]

### WWE (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: WWE (2015)")]

As an avid [professional wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling "Professional wrestling") fan,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell campaigned for a guest appearance on [WWE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE "WWE")'s weekly _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ program.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-27)

In May 2015, it was reported that he was set to wrestle [Stardust (Cody Rhodes)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") at WWE's [SummerSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SummerSlam_(2015) "SummerSlam (2015)") pay-per-view in August.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-HollywoodLifeWWE-26) Amell made his first WWE appearance on the May 25 episode of _Raw_, where he had a confrontation with Stardust.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-28) Amell returned to _Raw_ in early August; after being assaulted in the audience by Stardust, Amell got into the [ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_ring "Wrestling ring") to attack him until being contained by security. Following a [backstage segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Segment "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") with [Triple H](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_H "Triple H"), it was announced that [Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neville_(wrestler) "Neville (wrestler)") would team with Amell to face Stardust and [King Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wade_Barrett "Wade Barrett") at SummerSlam.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-29)

At the event on August 23, 2015, Amell and Neville defeated Barrett and Stardust in a [tag team match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_tag_team_match_types "Professional wrestling tag team match types"). Amell participated in the wrestling, and, behind the scenes, wrestlers were said to have been impressed with Amell's performance.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-31) Amell became friends with Rhodes, with whom he later also worked on _Arrow_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-BulletClub-32)

On December 21, 2015, Amell was awarded a [Slammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slammy "Slammy") for the "Celebrity Moment of the Year" for his dive onto Stardust during the match.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-33)

### Ring of Honor (2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Ring of Honor (2017)")]

Amell returned to professional wrestling for [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") on November 17, 2017, at [Survival of the Fittest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survival_of_the_Fittest_(2017) "Survival of the Fittest (2017)").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-34) On the day of the show, Amell joined the [Bullet Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullet_Club "Bullet Club")[faction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Stable "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"), and teamed with Cody Rhodes, [Kenny Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Omega "Kenny Omega"), and [The Young Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Young_Bucks "The Young Bucks") (Matt and Nick Jackson) in a five-on-four tag team match. They defeated [The Addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Addiction_(professional_wrestling) "The Addiction (professional wrestling)") ([Christopher Daniels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Daniels "Christopher Daniels") and [Frankie Kazarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankie_Kazarian "Frankie Kazarian")), [Flip Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_Gordon "Flip Gordon"), and [Scorpio Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpio_Sky "Scorpio Sky"), and Amell again participated in the wrestling, including being put through a table by The Addiction.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-35)

On August 6, 2018, it was announced that Amell would be competing at [All In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_In_(professional_wrestling_event) "All In (professional wrestling event)"), in his first-ever singles match, where he was defeated by Christopher Daniels.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-36)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

Amell has hosted a number of successful fundraising campaigns via the crowd funded merchandise platform [Represent.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Represent.com "Represent.com").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-38) In 2014, Amell partnered with the charity Fuck Cancer to raise almost a million dollars with the release of a T-shirt featuring his face on the front (with a Post-it note on his forehead and featuring the organization's name). He ended up selling over 60,000 shirts from this campaign.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-39) In January 2015, Amell launched his second Represent.com campaign featuring a word he made up, _Sinceriously_, to benefit two mental health charities: Paws and Stripes and Stand For The Silent.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In August 2015, Amell used his guest appearance on _[WWE Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_ with [Stardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") to raise funds via his third campaign for children's hospice Emily's House in Toronto. The campaign raised $300,000, and Amell and Stardust presented a cheque together at Emily's House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-40) During the Red Nose Day special of _[American Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Ninja\_Warrior "American Ninja Warrior")_, Amell donated $35,000 for completing all six obstacles, and an extra obstacle, the Salmon Ladder.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-41)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Stephen_Amell&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Amell married his first wife, fellow Canadian Carolyn Lawrence, on December 8, 2007, in Toronto.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-42) The couple divorced in 2010.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-43) Amell married actress and model [Cassandra Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassandra_Jean "Cassandra Jean") on December 25, 2012, in a private ceremony in [the Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Caribbean "The Caribbean"),[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-44) and for a second time in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") on May 26, 2013.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-45) The couple have a daughter who was born on October 15, 2013. They have a son, born May 13, 2022.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-46) Amell revealed on his Instagram that he became a dual citizen of Canada and the United States and took his U.S. citizenship oath in August 2022 at Dodger Stadium.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-47)

Amell's statements and behavior have occasionally drawn controversy. In September 2015, after a [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") student was arrested for [bringing a disassembled digital clock to his high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Mohamed_clock_incident "Ahmed Mohamed clock incident") in [Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving,_Texas "Irving, Texas"), Texas, Amell tweeted, "Stereotyping Texas isn't any better than stereotyping Ahmed".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-48) The post drew criticism online, prompting Amell to take a break from social media.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-51)

In 2018, Amell tweeted "my âpölògīés"[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-52) in response to criticism about his failure to use the [acute accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acute_accent "Acute accent") while tweeting singer [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé")'s name.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-54) After he was accused by online commenters of disrespecting [black names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_names "African-American names"), he said he had omitted the accent while being "lazy in the midst of a mediocre joke".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-55)

In 2020, during the [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter")[protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests"), Amell was criticized by comic book writer [Tee Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tee_Franklin "Tee Franklin") and others for saying that racism is a systemic problem but that he had not personally "seen it in action".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-56)

In 2021, Amell was asked to leave a [Delta Air Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Air_Lines "Delta Air Lines") flight traveling from Austin to Los Angeles for yelling at his wife.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-57) He later said he was intoxicated at the time.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-59)

In July 2023, Amell was criticized for comments he made at a fan convention regarding the [2023 SAG-AFTRA strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SAG-AFTRA_strike "2023 SAG-AFTRA strike"). While he expressed support for [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA") as his union, he called striking a "reductive negotiating tactic" and "myopic" and seemed to criticize that the strike banned him from promoting the second season of _Heels_.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-61) He later clarified his opinion, saying that while he does not like striking, he "[understands] fundamentally why we're here" and stated that his support for the union was unconditional and that he stood with them.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-62) Amell did not attend the _Arrow_ cast reunion on the picket line outside the Warner Bros. studio lot in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"), as he was in New York City at the time, but on the day of the reunion, he was photographed on the picket line in front of the [Warner Bros. Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Discovery "Warner Bros. Discovery") offices in New York and reportedly sent his regards to his former showrunners in California. [Marc Guggenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Guggenheim "Marc Guggenheim"), executive producer of _Arrow_ and organizer of the revival, interpreted his attendance in New York as a symbolic stand in solidarity.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Amell#cite_note-64)
